persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Amy, 45, visiting your mother, Ruth, 78, in Peoria, Illinois. Ruth takes blood pressure pills, goes for a walk every day, goes grocery shopping and to church, and she often forgets the pills. Her son David in Chicago worries about her. Today you are setting up Every Day on your mom's phone for her.

challenge.intro: Now you are Amy, setting up your mom's phone in Peoria. The app must start empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press: use what you learned. You do NOT need to send any real text message. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open Every Day. This app is not in the house erase list, so there is no 🧹 Start fresh link at the bottom. Instead: 1) If the welcome tour shows by itself, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, tap the ? button at the bottom right → '🎬 Take the tour again' → 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. This removes the six example cards. 2) If any cards are still there, tap '✏️ Change or remove a card' → tap the card's name → '🗑 Remove' → OK. Repeat until no cards are left. 3) Tap '⚙️ Settings · I’m OK text · day off' → 'Let someone know I’m OK'. If it says On, open it and tap 'Turn off'. Close Settings. The screen now says 'Make a card'.

tasks.text: Your mom takes a walk every day. Make a card for it.
tasks.hint: Use the card with the plus sign. Put the word walk in its name, and choose every day.

tasks.text: She takes blood pressure pills twice a day: in the morning and in the evening. Make ONE card for her pills that gets a separate tick for each time.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('dj_everyday_v1')||'null');if(!d||!Array.isArray(d.habits))return false;return d.habits.some(function(h){var ds=Array.isArray(h.doses)?h.doses:[];if(ds.length<2)return false;var l=ds.map(function(x){return String(x.label||'').toLowerCase()});return l.some(function(s){return s.indexOf('morn')>=0})&&l.some(function(s){return s.indexOf('even')>=0})})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Two separate cards is not right. Open one card and look for 'More than once a day? (pills)'.

tasks.text: She goes to church on Sundays only. Make a card for church that is due only on Sunday.
tasks.hint: Under 'How often?', choose 'On set days', and leave only Sun chosen.

tasks.text: She goes grocery shopping about three times a week, on any days she likes. Make a card for grocery shopping that fits.
tasks.hint: It is not every day. Look under 'How often?' for 'Some times a week'. Put the word grocery or shopping in its name.

tasks.text: Her son David (mobile 847-555-0142) wants to know she is OK each day. Set the app so it offers to tell David she is OK. Do not send a real message.
tasks.hint: Look in '⚙️ Settings' for 'Let someone know I’m OK'. Type David's name AND number, then Save.

tasks.text: Today she already took her walk. Show that it is done today.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('dj_everyday_v1')||'null');if(!d||!Array.isArray(d.habits))return false;var t=new Date();var k=t.getFullYear()+'-'+String(t.getMonth()+1).padStart(2,'0')+'-'+String(t.getDate()).padStart(2,'0');var lg=(d.log||{})[k]||{};return d.habits.some(function(h){return /walk/i.test(String(h.name||''))&&!!lg[h.id]})}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Tap the walk card itself. It turns gold with a tick.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: remembering small daily things (walk, pills, a call) by tapping a card when it is done
it counts how many days in a row you keep each one going
it can get an I am OK text ready for family far away

lines: Welcome. This short video explains Every Day: what it is for, and how to use it.
First, the problem. The small things in a day slip away. A short walk. Taking your pills. Calling someone. Drinking enough water.
Not because we don't care. It's because nothing reminds us, and nothing notices when we do them.
Every Day is for anyone, but it was made with older people in mind, and with family far away who like to know they are all right.
Here is the whole idea. Each small thing is a card, like a playing card. When you have done it today, you tap the card. That is all.
Everything is on one screen. Under the name is the helper line. It says what is still left to do today.
Under it are three numbers. Today shows how many of today's cards are done.
Best run is the most days in a row you have kept a card going. Perfect this week counts the days when every card was done.
Then the week, Monday to Sunday. A gold day means everything was done. The dot marks today.
Then the cards. Each has a picture, a name, and a big number: its run, how many days in a row it has been done.
Tap a card when it is done, and it turns gold with a tick. Tap it again to undo a mistake.
If a card says not today, it isn't due today, so it can't break the run. Finish every card due today, and the screen celebrates a perfect day.
To make a new card, scroll down and tap Add a card, the one with the plus sign.
Under What is it, type a few words, like Walk to the corner. Then tap a picture.
Then How often. On set days means every day, or only the days you tap, like only Sunday. Some times a week means, say, three times a week on any days you like.
Pills are special. Tap Yes, add times of day, and add a line for each time, like Morning and Evening. The card gets its own tick for each one.
Tap Save to keep it, or Cancel to leave everything as it was.
To change or remove a card later, tap Change or remove a card, then the card's name. Remove asks first.
Next to each card is history: its run, its best run ever, and the last four weeks. Green means done.
Now the button called Settings, I'm OK text, day off. Inside is Let someone know I'm OK.
Type the name and mobile number of one or two people, like a son or a daughter. Then choose when it offers: when you finish your last card, or at a time you pick.
Then the app gets a short text ready: I'm OK, and what was done today. It never sends by itself. You tap, your messages open, and you press Send.
Back in Settings is Sick day, day off. If you are unwell, take the day off and your runs stay safe. You can do this once every seven days.
How to start. The first time you open it, a short welcome tour shows you around. At the end, keep the six example cards, or start fresh with your own.
Then tap one card you have already done today, and change one example into something you really do.
Everything stays on this phone. There is no account and nothing to sign up for. Every Day comes with the Family membership, with as many pill cards as you need.
And when you open the app itself, the question mark button in the bottom corner has the tour and help any time.

daily.task: Tick today’s cards in Every Day as you do them — or add one new card for something you do every day.

explore.name: 🃏 Your cards
explore.find: Open Every Day. The cards are on the first screen.
explore.try: Tap a card to tick it, tap again to undo. Tick every card and watch what happens.

explore.name: 📊 Numbers at the top
explore.find: The top of the screen and the week row.
explore.try: Check Today, Best run and Perfect this week change when you tick and untick cards.

explore.name: ✏️ Change or remove a card
explore.find: Tap ✏️ Change or remove a card.
explore.try: Open a card: change its words, picture and days. Save. Try Cancel. Remove one (it asks first).

explore.name: ➕ Add a card
explore.try: Make one with a very long name, one with emoji, and try one with no name. Try “Some times a week”, and a pills card with three times a day. Try to add a 9th card.

explore.name: 📅 A card’s history
explore.find: In the change list, tap 📅 History.
explore.try: Look at the four weeks. Tap ✏️ Change it, then Close.

explore.name: ⚙️ Settings
explore.try: Set up the “I’m OK” text with a made-up name and number (try letters in the number). Look at the text — don’t send. Try the sick day.

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), 🏠 Start menu, 👪 My Circle, ✨ Ask an AI, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
